_meta.layout: 16 pairing-object scalars, 8 G1 commitments of 4 words (x_lo136, x_hi, y_lo136, y_hi), then sumcheck univariates; offsets in bytes
_meta.apply: take bases[base].proof, write each patchWords[i] at byte patchOffsets[i], cut to proofLength, verify against publicInputs
_meta.expect: reject = the verifier reverts or returns false; accept = it verifies
_meta.outOfScope: G2 mutations: the proof carries no G2 points and the verification key's are trusted

vectors.name: deposit/g1-coordinate-ge-p
vectors.reason: w1.x + p: a G1 coordinate must be < p (and it changes the transcript)

vectors.name: deposit/g1-off-curve
vectors.reason: w1.y flipped: the point is off the curve

vectors.name: deposit/fr-scalar-ge-r-sumcheck
vectors.reason: both verifiers reduce proof scalars mod r before hashing the transcript, so s + r reads as s: the proof bytes are malleable, the statement is not. Nothing keys on proof bytes (nullifiers bind public inputs), so this is recorded as a boundary (2.3d D6), not a defect
